body.statement: For arbitrary finite \(T,K,q\), can the projection of \(\{\mathbb E_D[\Phi_T\Phi_T^{\top}]:D\in\mathfrak D_T\}\) relevant to \(\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]\) be characterized by a lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient family of parity and positivity inequalities with explicit sign-orbit recovery, and can that characterization yield a quantitative finite-horizon bound \(|V_{T,K}-R_e^2N_q^2|\le c(K,q,R_g,R_e)/T\)?
body.justification: This exposes the genuinely unresolved general-order content instead of presenting a generic orbit SDP as a closed-form solution.
body.gap: Bandeira and Kunisky characterize degree-four pseudomoments rather than genuine binary-law moments, and Manchester's input-design lift has an approximation gap.
body.consumer: A lag-sized certificate would permit exact finite-sample design optimization for multi-lag N-of-1 targets without enumerating \(2^T\) paths.
